title: Multiple Regression Anatomy
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Move sliders for square feet, bedrooms, and age and watch the intercept and each coefficient-times-feature term add up to a predicted house price.

learningObjectives: Students will be able to explain how the intercept and each coefficient-times-feature term combine into one prediction, and interpret a coefficient as the change in the prediction for a one-unit increase in its feature with the other features held constant.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Labeled equation with feature sliders and a waterfall chart of each term's contribution
keyQuestions: When you move one slider, why do the other two terms stay the same?
What does the intercept represent, and why is it not a realistic house price?
Why is the age term red while the other two terms are green?
commonMisconceptions: The coefficient with the largest number belongs to the most important feature (coefficients have different units, so 150 per square foot and 10,000 per bedroom cannot be compared directly).
The intercept is the price of a typical house (it is the prediction when every feature is 0, which no real house has).
Changing one feature changes how much the other features contribute (in this model each term depends only on its own feature).
A negative coefficient means the model is wrong (it means the prediction falls as that feature rises).
assessmentOpportunities: Given the model Price = 50,000 + 150 × SqFt + 10,000 × Bedrooms − 1,000 × Age, students compute the prediction for a 2,000 square foot, 4-bedroom, 10-year-old house and explain what the coefficient −1,000 means, using the phrase "holding the other features constant".
